text: Writing clean code is a skill that separates good programmers from great ones. At its core, clean code is about readability—ensuring that anyone, including your future self, can understand what your code does without struggling. One essential practice is using clear naming conventions. For example, instead of naming a variable 'x', call it 'userAge' or 'totalPrice'. Good names tell the reader what the data represents. Another key idea is to keep functions small and focused. Each function should do one thing only, like calculating a discount or saving a record. This makes the code easier to test and reuse. Ultimately, clean code leads to better maintainability, meaning you can fix bugs and add new features quickly and safely.
